Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/5] Parallel process latent growth curve models showed that naturalistic developmental changes in nonreactivity tracked concomitant decreases in perceived stress and negative affect and increases in positive affect. [/page/9/Text/6] Finally, random intercept cross-lagged panel models indicated that within-person nonreactivity prospectively predicted within-person changes in perceived stress and positive affect, but not negative affect. [/page/9/Figure/3] Figure 3. Random intercept cross-lagged panel model with nonreactivity and positive affect. ... PA = positive affect.

sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/8/Text/8] This study is among the first to explicitly track naturalistic development of a dimension of mindfulness during adolescence and test how developmental change is associated with emotional well-being. Latent growth curve models indicated that, from 8th grade through 9th grade, adolescents matured in their capacity to become aware of yet remain nonreactive to difficult experiences.

ethnicity.evidence_source: [/page/8/Text/8] The pattern of developmental growth in nonreactivity was similar across gender, SES, and ethnicity.
